issues.legal_issue: The practice of a legal profession falls within the meaning of business in the ground for eviction based on a landlord’s need for a non-residential premises.
material_facts: The landlord was an advocate who sought possession of a non-residential premises to practise his profession.
The tenant used the premises to manufacture art jewellery.
The final court of fact found that the landlord bona fide required the premises to practise as an advocate, and an eviction order was passed.
issues.conclusion: The practice of law is business within the meaning of Section 10(3)(a)(iii) of the Andhra Pradesh Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1960, so the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The meaning of a word in an enactment must take its colour from the context in which it appears; its use or definition in another enactment is not a reliable guide, particularly where the enactments are not cognate. Business is capable of a broad meaning that includes activities occupying a person’s time, attention and labour for livelihood or profit. In the context of this generally applicable rent-control legislation, business includes the practice of a legal profession; excluding professional landlords would produce an anomalous result. The Court approved Re Williams’ Will Trusts, Chartered Bank of India, Australia and China v Williams, [1953] 1 All E.R. 536, and Taramal v Laxman Sewak Surey, 1971 MPLJ 888, and distinguished M.P. Sethurama Menon v Meenakshi Amma, AIR 1967 Kerala 88, Bangalore Water-Supply and Sewerage Board v R. Rajappa, [1978] 3 SCR 207, and Stuchbery v General Accident Fire and Life Assurance Corporation Ltd., [1949] 2 KBD 256, because those cases concerned different statutory contexts.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_case: A landlord seeks possession of a tenant’s premises through a rent-control eviction proceeding.
predicates.landlord_needs_nonresidential_premises_f: The landlord bona fide requires a non-residential premises to carry on a profession.
predicates.eviction_ground_covers_business_need: The applicable eviction ground permits a landlord to seek possession of a non-residential premises for a business need.
predicates.professional_practice_counts_as_business: A landlord’s practice of a profession qualifies as business for the purpose of the applicable eviction ground.

issues.definition: When a rent-control eviction proceeding concerns a landlord’s bona fide professional need for a non-residential premises and the eviction ground covers business needs, the professional practice counts as business.
